Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks. We're on it. Quick confirmation of deliverables by tomorrow EOD:  

1) One-paragraph narrative (below).
2) One annotated single-page diagram (attached PNG).
3) A compact egress assurance sheet (attached XLSX) listing allowed egress patterns and recommended firewall/IP ranges.

High-level narrative (use as-is or edit):
Redwood Inference separates customer data plane from Redwood control services by design. For Dedicated deployments we provision customer-dedicated GPU pools within the customer's VPC or private subnet consuming only customer-assigned IP space; runtime nodes handle inference and persist no long-term customer data outside configured object stores. The Redwood control plane (orchestrator, metrics ingestion, rollout APIs) runs in a logically separate, Redwood-managed environment and communicates with deployment agents over mutually authenticated TLS tunnels. For Private/on-prem deployments, control-plane functions can be operated via a customer-hosted control plane or a customer-peered private control plane — in either case, agents only accept signed commands and send telemetry over encrypted channels. Egress from the customer data plane is always explicit: either customer-managed (no Redwood egress), customer-approved peering to cloud services, or, when requested, tightly scoped outbound NAT through Redwood-managed egress with audit logging and per-tenant filtering.

Attachments: 
- [Attachment: redwood_data-plane-boundary_diagram_v1.png (image/png)] — single-page annotated view showing Dedicated vs Private flows.
- [Attachment: egress-assurance-matrix_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)] — matrix of egress options and evidence notes.

Notes / quick clarifications:
- KV cache (inference context cache) is kept in-process on runtime nodes and not shared across customers unless explicitly configured via a shared-cache opt-in; cache encryption at rest is supported for persistent layers.
- We will add control-plane hostname annotations per your request.

If you'd like, we can also produce a redacted packet that references specific SOC 2 controls for each assertion.

Maya / team — adding a few technical details to ensure the packet meets SIG expectations (please feel free to paste these into the 'system architecture' field):

- Mutual TLS + mTLS client certificates are used for control-plane-agent authentication; certificates are rotated on a schedule and can be integrated with customer PKI for Private control plane deployments.
- Control-plane connections are strictly outbound from the runtime agent to avoid inbound firewall openings; for Dedicated deployments inside a customer VPC we use egress-only rules and optional customer-managed peering.
- There is no cross-tenant routing inside the data plane: network namespaces + strict iptables/NIC-level segmentation prevent traffic crossing between tenant workloads.
- Audit logs (control-plane operations, model rollouts, API calls) are forwarded to a configurable log sink; for customers that require it we can push logs to the customer's SIEM or S3 bucket with agreed retention.
- Persistent KV stores (if enabled) are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK support) and in-flight encryption is TLS 1.3. Ephemeral in-memory caches do not persist to disk unless explicitly configured in sample workflows.

Attached: same diagram (PNG) with an extra layer showing mTLS and cert rotation, and an egress sheet that enumerates CIDR ranges and recommended firewall rules.

If you need packet captures or config snippets for firewall/peering on your side, we can prepare a redacted example.

Kimberly Park
